- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

ultracode You are a Senior UI/UX Architect, Frontend Engineer, and Responsive Web Design Expert.

Your task is to analyze the entire project (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, icons, and the attached SRS) and transform it into a premium enterprise-level B2B IT Equipment Rental website.

Tech Stack:
- HTML5
- CSS3
- Vanilla JavaScript
- No Bootstrap
- No Tailwind
- No React
- No backend changes

IMPORTANT:
- Preserve all existing functionality.
- Preserve all business logic.
- Preserve file names and folder structure.
- Do not remove any existing content unless it is clearly redundant.
- Improve only the frontend architecture, responsiveness, accessibility, animations, and user experience.

The website should look like it was designed by a professional UI/UX agency.

==================================
DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
==================================

Create a modern premium corporate UI with:

• Clean spacing
• Proper visual hierarchy
• Enterprise appearance
• Consistent typography
• Modern cards
• Better shadows
• Better hover effects
• Rounded corners where appropriate
• Smooth transitions
• Glassmorphism only where suitable
• Professional color usage
• Consistent border radius
• Proper icon alignment

==================================
RESPONSIVE REQUIREMENTS
==================================

The website must be fully responsive.

Support:

320px
375px
390px

1920px

No overflow.
No horizontal scrolling.
No broken layouts.
No overlapping elements.
No stretched cards.
No inconsistent spacing.

Everything should resize proportionally.

==================================
LAYOUT IMPROVEMENTS
==================================

Improve:

Navigation
Hero section
Product cards
Brand logos
Statistics
Buttons
Sections
Footer
Contact section
Forms
Cards
Grid layouts

Maintain consistent:

padding
margin
font size
line height
button height
card height
icon size
image ratio

==================================
TYPOGRAPHY
==================================

Create a complete typography scale.

Use consistent:

Heading sizes
Paragraph sizes
Font weights
Letter spacing
Line heights

Maintain proper readability on every screen.

==================================
CSS
==================================

Refactor CSS.

Remove:

duplicate styles
unused selectors
conflicting media queries

Use:

CSS variables
modular organization
mobile-first approach
consistent spacing scale

==================================
ANIMATIONS
==================================

Add tasteful animations only.

Examples:

fade in
slide up
hover elevation
button ripple
image zoom
counter animation
smooth scrolling
sticky navbar transition

Animations must be smooth and professional.

==================================
ACCESSIBILITY
==================================

Improve:

semantic HTML
ARIA labels
focus states
keyboard navigation
contrast ratio
image alt tags

==================================
PERFORMANCE
==================================

Optimize:

CSS
JavaScript
Images
Animation performance
Rendering

Avoid layout shifts.

==================================
CODE QUALITY
==================================

Follow:

HTML5 best practices
Modern CSS architecture
Clean JavaScript
Reusable components
Maintainable code
Production-ready structure

==================================
SRS ALIGNMENT
==================================

Use the SRS as the design reference.

The UI should reflect an enterprise B2B Rental Management System.

Design should communicate:

Trust
Professionalism
Reliability
Security
Scalability

==================================
OUTPUT
==================================

Analyze every page and every section.

Identify every UI/UX inconsistency.

Fix:
- alignment
- spacing
- font hierarchy
- responsiveness
- button consistency
- card consistency
- image sizing
- icon alignment
- section spacing
- mobile usability
- tablet usability
- desktop usability

Do not stop until the entire project has a consistent professional design.

Return production-ready HTML, CSS, and JavaScript while preserving existing functionality and file structure. Before making any changes, thoroughly review the entire project and the SRS to ensure you fully understand the user's requirements. Verify that all requested features, UI, UX, responsiveness, and functionality are covered. If anything is missing or inconsistent, fix it while preserving the existing functionality and project structure. Recheck the project after implementation to ensure every requirement has been satisfied.

- **Database:** Relational database (MySQL/PostgreSQL/MariaDB)
- **Integration:** RESTful API for integration with existing website
- **Security:** HTTPS encryption, role-based access control, input validation
- **Compatibility:** Responsive design for desktop and tablet use

### 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
1. **Integration Constraint:** Must integrate seamlessly with the existing website at `index.html`
2. **Technology Stack:** Should leverage existing web technologies where possible (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript)
3. **Data Migration:** Must accommodate import of existing inventory and customer data
4. **Brand Compliance:** Must comply with brand guidelines for all displayed OEM logos and product information
5. **Business Rules:** Must enforce B2B-only rental policy (no individual consumers)
6. **Regulatory:** Must comply with data protection regulations for customer information

### 2.6 User Documentation
- Administrator Guide
- Staff User Manual
- Customer Portal Guide
- API Documentation for website integration
- Troubleshooting FAQ

### 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies
1. The existing website will remain as the primary customer-facing interface
2. The RMS will provide APIs for the website to consume inventory and rental data
3. All customers are verified business entities (no individual consumers)
4. Initial inventory data will be migrated from existing records
5. The system will operate in a single timezone (IST - India Standard Time)

---

## 3. Specific Requirements

### 3.1 External Interface Requirements

#### 3.1.1 User Interfaces
- **Administrator Dashboard:** Web-based interface for system configuration and oversight
- **Staff Interface:** Web-based interface for rental operations, inventory management, and customer service
- **Customer Portal:** Secure web interface for customers to browse inventory, request rentals, and manage accounts
- **Responsive Design:** All interfaces must be responsive and accessible on desktop and tablet devices
- **Brand Consistency:** UI must align with the visual identity of the existing website

#### 3.1.2 Hardware Interfaces
- Barcode/RFID scanners for inventory tracking (optional)
- Receipt printers for on-site transactions
- Signature capture devices for delivery confirmations (optional)

#### 3.1.3 Software Interfaces
- **RESTful API:** For integration with the existing website to provide:
  - Real-time inventory availability
  - Product catalog information
  - Rental request submission
  - Customer account information (read-only for website)
- **Database:** MySQL 8.0+ or PostgreSQL 12+
- **Authentication:** Integration with LDAP/Active Directory optional for internal users
- **Payment Gateway:** Integration with payment processors (Stripe, Razorpay, PayPal) for online payments
- **Email Service:** Integration with SMTP service for automated notifications (SendGrid, AWS SES, etc.)

#### 3.1.4 Communications Interfaces
- HTTP/HTTPS for web interfaces
- REST/JSON for API communications
- SMTP for email notifications
- SMS gateway integration optional for SMS notifications

### 3.2 Functional Requirements

#### 3.2.1 User Management
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| UM-001 | The system shall support role-based access control with predefined roles: Administrator, Rental Manager, Sales Representative, Operations Staff, Accounting/Finance |
| UM-002 | The system shall allow administrators to create, modify, deactivate, and reactivate user accounts |
| UM-003 | The system shall enforce strong password policies (minimum 8 characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters) |
| UM-004 | The system shall support multi-factor authentication for administrator accounts |
| UM-005 | The system shall log all user login/logout activities and significant actions |
| UM-006 | The system shall support password reset functionality via email verification |

#### 3.2.2 Inventory Management
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| IM-001 | The system shall track inventory items with attributes: item ID, type (server/laptop/computer/firewall/printer/refurbished), brand, model, serial number, specifications, acquisition date, warranty information, condition (new/refurbished), location, and status (available/rented/maintenance/reserved) |
| IM-002 | The system shall support categorization of inventory by all major brands (Dell, HP, Lenovo, IBM, Asus, Acer, Canon, Cisco, Fortinet, Sophos, etc.) |
| IM-003 | The system shall track refurbished equipment separately with certification details and warranty information |
| IM-004 | The system shall allow bulk import of inventory data via CSV/Excel |
| IM-005 | The system shall generate unique identification numbers/tags for each inventory item |
| IM-006 | The system shall track equipment location (warehouse, customer site, in-transit, maintenance) |
| IM-007 | The system shall automate status updates based on rental transactions (rented → available upon return) |
| IM-008 | The system shall support barcode/QR code generation for inventory tracking |
| IM-009 | The system shall prevent rental of equipment under maintenance or repair |

#### 3.2.3 Customer Management
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| CM-001 | The system shall maintain customer profiles with: company name, contact person, email, phone, address, GST/VAT number, industry type (IT/manufacturing/business/startup/educational/BPO), credit limit, payment terms |
| CM-002 | The system shall validate that all customers are business entities (no individual consumers allowed) |
| CM-003 | The system shall track customer rental history, including all past and current rentals |
| CM-004 | The system shall allow categorization of customers by industry vertical for reporting purposes |
| CM-005 | The system shall store multiple contacts per customer account |
| CM-006 | The system shall flag customers with overdue payments or excessive late returns |
| CM-007 | The system shall support customer self-registration with admin approval workflow |

#### 3.2.4 Rental Management
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| RM-001 | The system shall allow customers to browse available inventory through the customer portal or website |
| RM-002 | The system shall allow customers to submit rental requests specifying equipment, quantities, rental period, delivery/pickup preferences |
| RM-003 | The system shall allow staff to create rental quotations based on customer requirements |
| RM-004 | The system shall generate rental agreements/contracts with terms and conditions, pricing, and SLA details |
| RM-005 | The system shall track rental equipment allocation to specific customer orders |
| RM-006 | The system shall schedule and track equipment delivery and pickup logistics |
| RM-007 | The system shall support rental extensions and early terminations with prorated billing |
| RM-008 | The system shall enforce minimum and maximum rental periods based on equipment type |
| RM-009 | The system shall require security deposits for high-value equipment (servers, enterprise equipment) |
| RM-010 | The system shall automate equipment readiness checks before dispatch |
| RM-011 | The system shall generate pickup/delivery checklist for operations staff |
| RM-012 | The system shall track equipment condition at checkout and check-in |

#### 3.2.5 Billing and Invoicing
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| BI-001 | The system shall generate invoices based on rental duration, equipment rates, applicable taxes, and additional charges |
| BI-002 | The system shall support different billing models: daily, weekly, monthly rates |
| BI-003 | The system shall calculate and apply taxes (GST) according to Indian tax regulations |
| BI-004 | The system shall support security deposit collection and refund processing |
| BI-005 | The system shall generate periodic invoices for ongoing long-term rentals |
| BI-006 | The system shall track payment status (pending, paid, partial, overdue) |
| BI-007 | The system shall apply late fees for overdue payments per company policy |
| BI-008 | The system shall support multiple payment methods: bank transfer, credit card, online payment gateways |
| BI-009 | The system shall generate payment receipts for all transactions |
| BI-010 | The system shall provide aging reports for accounts receivable |
| BI-011 | The system shall allow adjustment of invoices for damages, late returns, or early termination |

#### 3.2.6 Maintenance Management
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| MM-001 | The system shall track maintenance schedules for all equipment based on manufacturer recommendations or usage |
| MM-002 | The system shall allow scheduling of preventive maintenance and track completion |
| MM-003 | The system shall manage repair workflows: issue reporting, diagnosis, repair estimation, parts replacement, and completion |
| MM-004 | The system shall track warranty claims and coordinate with OEMs for warranty repairs |
| MM-005 | The system shall equipment available for rental only after maintenance/repair completion and quality check |
| MM-006 | The system shall maintain maintenance history for each equipment item |
| MM-007 | The system shall generate maintenance reports and forecasts |

#### 3.2.7 Reporting and Analytics
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| RA-001 | The system shall provide dashboard showing key metrics: utilization rates, revenue, active rentals, pending maintenance |
| RA-002 | The system shall generate utilization reports by equipment type, brand, and model |
| RA-003 | The system shall provide revenue reports by time period, customer, and equipment category |
| RA-004 | The system shall track customer lifetime value and rental frequency |
| RA-005 | The system shall provide aging reports for accounts receivable and equipment maintenance |
| RA-006 | The system shall generate equipment lifecycle reports to inform procurement decisions |
| RA-007 | The system shall support export of reports in PDF, Excel, and CSV formats |
| RA-008 | The system shall provide real-time inventory availability dashboard |

#### 3.2.8 Customer Portal
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| CP-001 | The customer portal shall allow authenticated customers to browse available inventory with real-time availability |
| CP-002 | The customer portal shall allow customers to submit rental requests with equipment selection, quantities, and rental period |
| CP-003 | The customer portal shall allow customers to view their current and past rentals |
| CP-004 | The customer portal shall allow customers to view and download invoices and payment receipts |
| CP-005 | The customer portal shall allow customers to make online payments for invoices |
| CP-006 | The customer portal shall allow customers to request rental extensions or early termination |
| CP-007 | The customer portal shall provide notifications for upcoming returns, payments, and contract expirations |

| ID | Requirement Description |

| WI-002 | The API shall provide real-time inventory availability for display on the website |

#### 3.3.1 Performance Requirements
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|

| PF-002 | The system shall support concurrent users: 50+ staff users, 100+ customer portal users |
| PF-003 | Database queries for inventory search shall return results within 2 seconds |
| PF-004 | The system shall generate standard reports within 10 seconds for datasets up to 10,000 records |

#### 3.3.2 Safety and Security Requirements
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| SR-001 | All data transmission shall use HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ encryption |
| SR-002 | Passwords shall be stored using strong, salted hashing (bcrypt or equivalent) |
| SR-003 | The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) for all functions |
| SR-004 | The system shall log all access to sensitive data (customer information, financial data) |
| SR-005 | The system shall implement session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity |
| SR-006 | The system shall validate all input to prevent SQL injection and XSS attacks |
| SR-007 | The system shall encrypt sensitive data at rest (PII, financial information) |
| SR-008 | The system shall support regular automated backups with point-in-time recovery |

#### 3.3.3 Security and Privacy Requirements
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|

| PP-003 | The system shall provide customers with access to their own data upon request |
| PP-004 | The system shall allow customers to request deletion of their data in accordance with applicable laws |

| ID | Requirement Description |

| OR-002 | Scheduled maintenance shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (2AM-5AM IST) with prior notification |
| OR-003 | The system shall provide clear error messages to users without exposing system internals |
| OR-004 | The system shall support multiple languages (English primary, with capability for Hindi localization) |
| OR-005 | The system shall be deployable on cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) or on-premise servers |

#### 3.3.5 Maintainability and Support Requirements
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| MS-001 | The system shall be designed with modular architecture for ease of maintenance |
| MS-002 | Code shall be well-documented and follow established coding standards |
| MS-003 | The system shall support automated testing (unit, integration, end-to-end) |
| MS-004 | The system shall provide administrative tools for database maintenance and diagnostics |
| MS-005 | Documentation shall be provided for installation, configuration, administration, and troubleshooting |

#### 3.3.6 Portability Requirements
| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|
| PT-001 | The web application shall be compatible with: Chrome 80+, Firefox 75+, Safari 13+, Edge 80+ |
| PT-002 | The system shall support responsive design for tablet and desktop browsers |
| PT-003 | The system shall be deployable on standard LAMP/WAMP/LAPP stacks |
| PT-004 | The database schema shall be portable between MySQL and PostgreSQL with minimal changes |

| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|

| ID | Requirement Description |
|----|------------------------|

| CL-002 | Rental agreements generated by the system shall include standard terms and conditions compliant with Indian Contract Act |
